newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Argentina lowers tax collection estimate for Feb.
newsitem.headline: Argentina lowers tax collection estimate for Feb.

text.p: Argentina's government lowered Wednesday its estimate for tax collection in February to between $3.6 and $3.7 billion from $3.8 billion.

"Judging by the tax collected until the middle of this month collections will be between $3.6 billion and $3.7 billion for all of February which implies a rise of around 10 percent from the same month last year," Guillermo Rodriguez Use, undersecretary for tax policy, told reporters.

The government had previously forecast tax collections of $3.8 billion in February. In January tax collection totalled $4.36 billion, 13.9 percent higher than in December and 12.7 percent higher than the same month in 1995.
Use added that in March collections would be lower than in February "because in March tax accrued from February is paid, it is the shortest month and includes Easter."
"Either way these levels of collections have been agreed with the International Monetary Fund (IMF)," said Use.
Argentina has agreed with the IMF on a deficit of $1.04 billion for the first quarter of the year and $3.0 billion for all of 1997.
